title: From One Forecast to a Thousand Futures
summary: My next research direction: using diffusion models to generate thousands of joint solar and wind scenarios, including Europe's dark, windless Dunkelflaute weeks.
imageAlt: Illustration of many possible solar and wind generation paths fanning out from today, with a dark winter period highlighted where output drops close to zero
titleMarkup: From one forecast to *a thousand futures.*
dek: A single forecast tells you the most likely outcome. Planning a renewable grid also needs the unlikely ones. This is how I want to use diffusion models to generate realistic solar and wind scenarios, extreme winter weeks included.

title: How to Start Researching One Topic
summary: How I turned a broad interest in sustainable energy into one research question, a dataset, and a published paper.
imageAlt: Abstract illustration of many scattered ideas narrowing into one focused question and a solar and wind generation chart
dek: Every research project I have done began the same way: with a subject far too big to study. Mine was sustainable energy. This is how I turned it into one question, one dataset, and eventually a published paper.

title: Building RAG Systems You Can Trust
summary: Six practical decisions that make retrieval-augmented generation more grounded, testable, and useful.
imageAlt: Abstract diagram of documents flowing through a layered retrieval system into a grounded answer
dek: A good RAG system is not defined by a clever prompt. It is defined by whether it retrieves the right evidence, cites it clearly, and behaves honestly when the evidence is weak.

title: Renewable Energy Consumption on Solar and Wind Energy Prediction Using Deep Learning and Generative AI
summary: My published paper on forecasting solar and wind energy production with feature selection, machine learning, an LSTM, and explainable AI.
imageAlt: Illustration of solar panels and wind turbines under the sun, with a forecast chart of solar and wind generation
titleMarkup: Renewable Energy Consumption on Solar and Wind Energy Prediction Using Deep Learning and *Generative AI.*
dek: A summary of my first published paper, written with four co-authors: what we set out to answer, how we approached it, and what we found.
